title: "Submodules"

# Submodule Mechanics: Add, Update, Clone

After this page you can attach another Git repository at a path and record **which commit** it should be.

## A submodule is a nested repository plus a gitlink

`desk-api` might need a shared `desk-lib` history without merging the trees. A **submodule** stores a commit hash in the parent tree (a **gitlink**, mode `160000`) and a URL in `.gitmodules`.

```text
 desk-api  (superproject)
 ├── README.md
 ├── src/ping.py
 └── src/desk-lib/          gitlink 160000 → commit 9fceb02 of desk-lib
         └── (nested .git)

 desk-lib  (its own history)
 A ← B ← 9fceb02    ← the hash the parent pins
```

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git submodule add ~/desk/desk-lib src/desk-lib
git status
git commit -m "chore: add desk-lib submodule"
```

`.gitmodules` is a tracked file:

```gitconfig
[submodule "src/desk-lib"]
    path = src/desk-lib
    url = /home/ada/desk/desk-lib
```

On Linux use an SSH URL for anything you will clone elsewhere (`git@host:ada/desk-lib.git`). A path only works on this machine.

## Clone a superproject

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules <url> desk-api
# or after a plain clone:
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Without `--recurse-submodules` / `update --init`, the path exists as an empty directory.

## Update the pin

```bash
cd src/desk-lib
git fetch
git switch main
git pull --ff-only
cd ../..
git add src/desk-lib
git commit -m "chore: bump desk-lib"
```

The parent records a **new gitlink hash**. Pulling the parent does not move the submodule until `git submodule update`.

## Pitfalls

- Committing in the submodule and forgetting to push it: the parent points at a hash nobody else can fetch.
- Editing files in `src/desk-lib` while detached: `git switch -c` in the submodule first.
- Nested submodules: `--recursive` on clone and update.

If the team is small and `desk-lib` changes with `desk-api` every day, a **monorepo** (chapter 15) or a copy may hurt less. Submodules shine when the nested project has its own release cycle.
